subject: PayGrid — model fit eval follow-up & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: PayGrid — post-call recap: eval plan + parity thresholds

Hi Ellen — thanks for the call earlier. Great context on PayGrid’s transaction-enrichment use case and the current in-house baseline. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from today’s call:
- Goal: Replace parts of PayGrid’s proprietary intent classifier and enrichment pipeline with an open-model-backed path for cost and latency gains while maintaining parity on quality.
- Baseline: "PayGrid-Baseline-v1" (your internal model) — team cares about intent accuracy and hallucination rates on high-value flows.
- Primary concerns: regression on edge prompts, predictable latency under 99th pct loads, and data handling/audit logs.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) Data & prompts: you share 2k de-identified examples + priority prompt set (we've attached the prompt CSV we used in the call).
2) Baseline run: Redwood runs PayGrid-Baseline-v1 on the set to produce reference metrics (intent accuracy, micro-F1, hallucination false-positive rate, top-3 NDCG for enrichment).
3) Open-model candidates: run the same tests on 3 open candidates we recommend: LLaMA-3-13B (8-bit quant), Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a tuned LLaMA-2-70B distilled variant.
4) Acceptance thresholds (proposed): intent accuracy within 3 percentage points of baseline OR better; hallucination rate <= baseline + 1.5pp; NDCG@3 within 5% relative. Latency target: p95 inference <= 220ms on your target payload (we can adjust based on sequence length).
5) Readout: annotated examples where open models regress, runbook for mitigation (prompt-engineering, light fine-tune, caching).

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Benchmark report (PDF) with per-model metrics and failure cases — attached.
- Prompt set CSV (attached).
- Shared Drive with raw inference logs and sample annotations: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-paygrid-evals
- HubSpot deal record for tracking: https://hubspot.com/deal/PG-2026-117

Next steps (suggested):
- You (PayGrid) to drop the de-identified sample set + any high-priority prompts by Friday 2026-02-13.
- Redwood to run baseline + open-model runs and deliver a draft report by 2026-02-20.
- Quick sync the week of 2026-02-23 to review results and decide on a short pilot (Dedicated capacity offer available if latency/cost tradeoffs look good).

Questions for you / items to confirm:
- Are the acceptance thresholds above aligned with your risk tolerance? (intent accuracy delta of 3pp, NDCG within 5%).
- Any additional compliance evidence you need (SOC2 artifact we can surface)?

Attachments: paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv, paygrid_openmodel_bench_results.pdf

Thanks — happy to adjust timelines if you need more time on the data share.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@paygrid.com>, Samir Khanna <samir.khanna@paygrid.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid — post-call recap: eval plan + parity thresholds

Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap and the attachments. This aligns well with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications: 

1) On acceptance thresholds: intent accuracy within 3pp is reasonable but we’re more sensitive on false positives for enrichment (the downstream billing rules break if hallucination rate increases). Can you explain how you measure "hallucination rate" for this evaluation?

2) Data share: we have a de-identified set of ~2.5k rows; Oliver will drop the S3 link by EOD today.

3) Pilot scope: assuming parity, would Redwood be open to a 30-day pilot limited to 100k transactions/month on Dedicated capacity? We want predictable latency.

Looping in Samir (ops) and Oliver (data) for logistics.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Product, PayGrid
ellen.park@paygrid.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 13:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid — post-call recap: eval plan + parity thresholds

Ellen — great, thanks for the signal and for sharing the dataset. Quick answers: 

How we measure hallucination rate: 
- We run model outputs through an automated detector tuned for entity hallucination (precision-focused) and then sample ~200 model outputs for human annotation to estimate the false-positive rate. For this eval we’ll report both the automated detector rate and the human-verified sample rate. The acceptance threshold we proposed (<= baseline + 1.5pp) uses the human-verified estimate as the canonical metric.

Pilot & Dedicated: 
- Yes, we’re open to a 30-day Dedicated pilot at the 100k tx/month scope. Aditya will follow up separately on commercial terms and a draft mutual action plan.

Proposed tweaks to the evaluation:
- Add a "sensitive prompts" slice (we’ve baked this into the attached CSV) to surface regressions quickly.
- We'll include a small, targeted prompt-rewrite attempt for top 20 failure cases to show how performance recovers with minimal engineering.

Timeline reminder: once we get the S3 link we’ll start baseline + open-model runs and aim to share the draft report by 2026-02-20.

References:
- Draft benchmark report (attached) — has per-model confusion matrices and a failure-case appendix.
- Internal ticket for the eval run: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4567

— Marissa

- We can offer a discounted Dedicated pilot rate for the 30-day, 100k tx scope (I’ll send a draft SOW + pricing today).
- If PayGrid needs strict SLA language for p95 latency during the pilot, we can add a short-term SLA in the pilot SOW; details in the SOW.
